item.title: FDO Conferences
item.description:
List of conferences

The FDO Forum sees it as one of its major tasks to organise regular conferences (1 to 2 years) to regularly bring the FDO community, which consists of a wide spectrum of data scientists, data stewards, data infrastructure builders, data application developers, and data policy experts.

2026 - Vienna, Austria

  • The third FDO conference was held from 25 to 27 March 2026 at TU Wien in Austria. The Save the Date announcement and the call for papers were available on the conference page.

2024 - Berlin, Germany

  • The second FDO conference was held in March 2024 in Berlin with the focus on the FDO specifications and the increasing number of implementations applications. The conference showed that many teams are working in isolation. A summary statement about the summit can be found here.

2022 - Leiden, Germany

-The first FDO conference was held in October 2022 in Leiden with as major goal to bring together the interested community to interact about FDOs, to find a common understanding and to discuss first specifications and applications.

item.title: Open Science in Practice: A Community Perspective
item.description:
The State of Open Science Today

Open science is no longer a fringe movement. Across the globe, funding agencies, universities, and research institutions are mandating open access to publications and data. But what does open science look like in practice?

We spoke with researchers from three different fields to find out how they are navigating the transition to more open ways of working.

item.title: Introducing FAIR Data Principles
item.description:
What are FAIR Data Principles?

FAIR stands for Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable. These principles were first published in 2016 and have since become the gold standard for scientific data management.

The goal of FAIR is to make data more useful — not just for humans, but also for machines. In an era of big data and automated analysis, having well-structured, well-described data is more important than ever.

Executive Committee

The members of the Executive Committee (EC) are appointed by the Steering Committee (SC) and have the following tasks:

  • prepare and chair the SC and Advisory Committee (AC) meetings and create the reports,
  • stimulate FDOF discussions and processes based on deep insights and engagement,
  • turn SC decisions into actions and bring in AC’s advice,
  • take care of the secretarial tasks (website, email lists, etc.),
  • check whether the tasks can be managed given the voluntary basis and restricted funding of FDOF,
  • makes tactical or short fuse decisions related to carrying out the general direction from the SC,
  • draft the FDO Bulletin as a general and regular note to the FDO community.

Steering Committee

The Steering Committee (SC) has the core task in the organisation. It is the decision-making body of the FDOF that:

  • steers the internal activities of the FDO Forum based on a governance structure and
  • adapt its structure where needed such as,
    • starting new Working Groups and Task Forces and finishing old ones,
    • checking the state of the Working Groups and Task Forces,
    • renew its membership on a regular basis in an open process,
  • maintains a strategic view based on deep insights of their members,
  • continues developing the FDO community and bringing active people together,
  • promotes the collaboration with initiatives with similar and related goals,
  • looks for improved funding opportunities to strengthen its organisational capacity,
  • appoints co-chairs (Executive Committee) that organise the SC work.

The decision making process in the SC will be guided by the principles of collaboration and consensus.

item.title: About Us
item.description:
Who We Are

We are a team of researchers, developers, and advocates working to build fair and open digital infrastructure.

Our Mission

Our mission is to advance principles of openness, fairness, and transparency across research, data, and digital systems.

Organizing the International FAIR Digital Objects (FDO) Community

The FAIR Digital Object Forum (FDOF) is organizing a plattform to advance the specification and application of FAIR Digital Objects (FDO). The objective is to increase the basic interoperability between the many repositories and dataspaces worldwide and to achieve a better coherence amongst the increasing number of initiatives working on FDO-based designs, implementations and applications in research, industry and other sectors.

item.title: FDO Specifications
item.description:
UPDATE 2026: A new formal specification is currently developed here

The following table includes all official documents on FDOs which the FDO Forum has released. All documents followed the official process as ligned out in the FDO Process Document. The first documents describe the core requirement specifications of the FDOs, while the others explain some details to better understand FDOs. The most Important documents are:

  • FDO Requirement specifications – a comprehensive list of FDO specifications endorsed by the FDOF
  • Data FDO – a short and easy to read primer of the specifications for FDOs that contain data
  • FDO Overview – an overview about the various documents on FDO
  • Implementation of Attributes, Types, Profiles and Registries – a comprehensive document describing details about types and registries.
